newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - April 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif unfolded a wide-ranging agriculture package at a farmers convention, substantially increasing the support prices of wheat, rice and oil seed, and abolishing the general sales tax on certified cotton seed.

- Three people, including a policeman, were killed and five wounded in a shootout between supporters of rival candidates at a female polling station during by-elections for a National Assembly seat in the suburb of Peshawar.

- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan told the Senate (upper house) that the timely action of intelligence agencies defeated the plot to kill Palestine President Yasser Arafat during his visit to Islamabad last month.
- Abbas Gokal, a Pakistani shipping magnet, was found guilty of defrauding the collapsed Bank of Credit and Commerce International of 750 million sterling pounds.

- The Deputy Prime Minister of Australia Tim Fischer said his government has accepted Pakistan's proposal to enter into an investment promotion and protection agreement to realise the potentials of bilateral trade.
- A marginal devaluation of the rupee is on the cards, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz told the National Assembly but did not say how soon it would be.
- Pakistan's foreign currency reserves dropped to $780 million from $930 million on March 28 on account of debt repayments.
- A mission of the International Monetary Fund is likely to visit Pakistan in May, sources said.
